text: Tu viens avec nous ce soir ?
glossEn: Are you coming with us tonight?

text: Qu'est-ce que tu fais ce week-end ?
glossEn: What are you doing this weekend?

notes: Marker: tu-imperative Appelle plus T-pronoun tu.

glossEn: Did you see the game yesterday?
notes: Marker: colloquial contraction T'as (tu as); doubly casual.
Marker: V-pronoun vous with conditional pourriez, plus the vous-form formula s'il vous plaît; V-form maps to polite.
Marker: V-pronoun vous with the address term madame confirming a singular addressee.

text: Bonjour, monsieur, que puis-je faire pour vous ?
glossEn: Hello, sir, what can I do for you?
notes: Marker: address term monsieur plus V-pronoun vous.

text: Est-ce que vous pourriez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
notes: Marker: V-pronoun vous with pourriez and s'il vous plaît.

glossEn: Thanks a lot! You're really nice.
notes: Trap: merci is a fossilized courtesy formula and sets no register; the contraction T'es (tu es) fixes the sentence as casual.

text: Passe-moi le sel, s'il te plaît.
notes: Trap: a 'please' formula does not make the sentence polite; here the formula itself is T-inflected (s'il TE plaît) and the imperative Passe is the tu-form, so the sentence is casual.
Trap: the quoted tu-imperative appelle-moi is casual, but the frame's vous-imperative Dites addresses the hearer politely; the frame's register governs.

text: Le train pour Lyon part à huit heures.
glossEn: The train to Lyon leaves at eight.
notes: Third-person statement with no addressee and no T/V form.

text: Il pleut souvent en Bretagne au printemps.
glossEn: It often rains in Brittany in spring.

text: Ce restaurant est fermé le lundi.
glossEn: This restaurant is closed on Mondays.
